patterns/09-heaps/01-k-smallest-lesson.i.first:
# 01. Heaps

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** A heap keeps the smallest value at the front. `heapq` implements a min-heap on a list.

**After this lesson you can:** keep a heap of the best k values so far; return them without a full sort.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [heapq](../../course/08-collections-module/04-heapq-lesson.ipynb)

patterns/10-trees/01-traversals-lesson.i.first:
# 01. Tree traversals

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** A binary tree node has a value, a left child, and a right child. Preorder visits the node, then the left, then the right.

**After this lesson you can:** walk a binary tree in order, preorder, or postorder; choose recursion or an explicit stack.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Classes](../../course/11-classes/01-classes-lesson.ipynb), [Nested data](../../course/09-recursion/02-structures-lesson.ipynb)

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** Land is `"1"`. Water is `"0"`.

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** A graph here is a list of edges. Two nodes are connected when an edge joins them, in either direction.

About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Island sizes](01-island-sizes-lesson.ipynb), [Nested data](../../course/09-recursion/02-structures-lesson.ipynb)

patterns/12-backtracking/01-subsets-less.first:
# 01. Backtracking

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** Backtracking tries a choice, recurses, then undoes the choice. For subsets, each value is either in the subset or not.

**After this lesson you can:** build subsets by choose-or-skip decisions; backtrack when a branch is done.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Lists](../../course/04-collections/01-lists-lesson.ipynb), [Functions](../../course/05-functions/01-definitions-lesson.ipynb), [Base case](../../course/09-recursion/01-base-case-lesson.ipynb)

patterns/13-dynamic-programming/02-circl.first:
# 02. Circle houses

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** You cannot rob two adjacent houses. At each house the best total is the better of two choices: skip it and keep the previous best, or rob it and add it to the best from two houses back.

**After this lesson you can:** reuse overlapping subproblems around a circular choice; avoid double-counting the wrap.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Min cost](01-min-cost-lesson.ipynb), [Memoization](../../course/09-recursion/04-memoization-lesson.ipynb)

patterns/13-dynamic-programming/03-combi.first:
# 03. Combinations

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** Let `fewest[amount]` be the fewest coins that sum to that amount. Each coin that fits updates it: one coin plus the fewest coins for the remainder.

**After this lesson you can:** count or list combinations with a DP table; see how order of loops changes the meaning.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Circle](02-circle-lesson.ipynb), [Memoization](../../course/09-recursion/04-memoization-lesson.ipynb)

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** A trie is a tree of letters. Each node has a map from a character to the next node.

**After this lesson you can:** insert and search words in a trie; share prefixes instead of scanning a flat list.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Dicts](../../course/04-collections/03-dicts-lesson.ipynb), [Classes](../../course/11-classes/01-classes-lesson.ipynb)

patterns/15-design/01-tiny-set-lesson.ip.first:
# 01. A small set

**Tier:** Deep. **Why you'd use this:** An LRU cache holds at most `capacity` keys. `get` returns the value or `-1`.

**After this lesson you can:** support insert, remove, and random get in expected constant time; pick the right backing structures.
About 20 minutes. **Uses:** [Dicts](../../course/04-collections/03-dicts-lesson.ipynb), [Classes](../../course/11-classes/01-classes-lesson.ipynb)
